key_insight: DexTacWAM adds touch to world-action models, letting a robot reason about contact-rich manipulation that vision alone cannot fully observe. By treating each fingertip separately and combining tactile information with pose awareness, it can better predict and act in dexterous tasks.
problem_solved: Vision-centric world models struggle with dexterous manipulation because key contact dynamics are hidden or ambiguous in images. This paper addresses the need for a model that can represent and use tactile feedback during action planning and prediction.
method: Encodes tactile input from each fingertip independently instead of treating touch as a single global signal.
Uses a finger- and pose-aware tactile compressor to aggregate fingertip features into a compact latent representation.
Injects the tactile latent into a World-Action Model to improve video prediction and action generation for manipulation.
impact: For AI and robotics practitioners, this work shows how to integrate tactile sensing into predictive control models for more reliable grasping and manipulation. It is especially relevant for tasks where small contact changes determine success, such as in-hand manipulation and object reorientation.

paper_title: DexTacWAM: A Visuo-Tactile World-Action Model for Dexterous Manipulation
paper_authors: Haoran Yuan, Zekai Wang, Boning Shao, Haoran Lu, Trevor Darrell
